LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 15.3.1 INTERJECTIONS OF SURPRISE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Language Use 15.3.1 Interjections of surprise
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 15.3.1 Interjections of surprise, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: howing surprise while learners with blindness be given one on one demonstration, clear verbal 1. How can you tell that someone is surprised?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 15.3.1 Interjections of surprise together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy-A learner interacts with digital devices with assistive technologies to search for emojis showing surprise.

● Creativity and imagination-A learner makes different familiar faces showing surprise.

Values:
Respect (acceptance) a learner understands and appreciates others during group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills– (effective communication): A learners uses interjections correctly in communication.

Link to other learning Areas:

The learner uses the knowledge of interjections of surprise to learn similar concept in Kiswahili Language and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Textbooks in appropriate print

• Braille reference materials

• Audio recording

• Digital devices with assistive technology
